newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks rise on new government optimism.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks rise on new government optimism.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose 0.74 percent on Wednesday with investors responding optimistically to news of a government change, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 1.13 points to 153.39 points.
"The factor of change was the only factor that raised the market today," said one broker.
"Investors are hopeful that the newly designated Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, who was the original man behind the peace process, was returning back to fulfil his promises," he added.

King Hussein of Jordan has dismissed Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti and replaced him with Majali, a veteran former premier who signed Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel, officials said on Wednesday.
Turnover of 402,796 dinars ($568,922) was dominated by investor demand on a handful of stocks and a few stocks performed well on the back of improved investor optimism, they said.
Arab Bank rose 4.50 dinars to 256 dinars in minimal trade worth 45,670 dinars.
Uncertainty about the fate of Arab-Israeli peace making has recently shaken confidence on the bourse, often a barometer of sentiment in the Middle East peace process.
Dar al Dawa drug firm, which was the busiest stock, rose 2.08 percent to 4.90 dinars in trade worth 106,385 dinars.
The second busiest, Unified Company, rose 0.10 dinars to 1.73 dinars in lower trading worth 45,670 dinars.
Overall rising shares outnumbered losers by 26 to ten. Another three shares traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange rose 0.56 percent to 80.43 points, 3.56 percent down from the start of the year.
